name: Property & Fire Restoration
summary: First notice of loss response, claim documentation, drying logs, and job updates.

automations.title: First Notice of Loss Response Automation
automations.summary: The moment a new loss is reported, by phone, web form, or insurance referral, this automation automatically dispatches the on-call crew, opens a job…
steps: The moment a new loss is reported, by phone, web form, or insurance referral, this automation automatically dispatches the on-call crew, opens a job file, and sends the customer a confirmation with the crew's estimated arrival time.
Response speed within the first hours affects both the extent of the damage and whether the job gets won over a competitor, and this automation removes the manual steps that eat into that window.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, a dispatch manager spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Insurance Claim Documentation Assembler
automations.summary: As technicians log moisture readings, photos, and scope of work in the field, this automation automatically compiles it into the documentation…
steps: As technicians log moisture readings, photos, and scope of work in the field, this automation automatically compiles it into the documentation package required by insurance adjusters.
The time between job completion and claim approval shrinks because the paperwork is already assembled instead of pieced together after the fact.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a claims coordinator spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Drying Equipment Monitoring Log
automations.summary: For water damage jobs, this automation automatically tracks daily moisture readings against drying targets and flags any room not progressing on…
steps: For water damage jobs, this automation automatically tracks daily moisture readings against drying targets and flags any room not progressing on schedule.
Equipment doesn't get left running, and billed, longer than the job actually requires simply because no one was watching the readings closely enough.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a project manager handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Job Milestone Customer Update
automations.summary: As a restoration job moves through its stages, mitigation, demolition, reconstruction, this automation automatically sends the homeowner a status…
steps: As a restoration job moves through its stages, mitigation, demolition, reconstruction, this automation automatically sends the homeowner a status update at each milestone.
The anxious \"what's happening with my house\" calls that pile up during a stressful time drop off because the homeowner already has the answer.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a customer service coordinator is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

automations.title: Subcontractor Invoice Reconciliation
automations.summary: As subcontractor invoices come in for a restoration job, this automation automatically checks them against the original scope of work and flags any…
steps: As subcontractor invoices come in for a restoration job, this automation automatically checks them against the original scope of work and flags any charges outside that scope for review before they're rolled into the final insurance billing.
Charges that don't belong in the claim get caught before they become a dispute with the insurer later.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a project accountant re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: DASH or a job costing system
